answer.rationale: Competitive pricing pressure on SMB creates a race-to-the-bottom dynamic that exp_73 proved is unsustainable—discounted SMB cohorts fail at renewal. Rather than match competitor pricing (which contradicts your primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue), redirect focus to enterprise accounts where memory_44 shows sales-assisted flows outperform self-serve on pipeline quality and conversion. This simultaneously (1) protects revenue from accounts with structural stickiness, (2) avoids the retention cliff documented in exp_73, and (3) leverages complementary wins in simplified onboarding (memory_86) and activation messaging (memory_91) to accelerate time-to-value for enterprise prospects. A standard experiment on enterprise-focused sales assistance lets you build pipeline resilience while price-sensitive SMB churn stabilizes. This preserves long-term unit economics and does not rely on memory gaps—all reasoning chains are grounded in archived data. Risk of churn in price-sensitive SMB segment remains, but accepting that segment's exit preserves the higher-LTV enterprise growth trajectory.
